title: Create trustworthy sample labels
intro: Two near-identical fluorescence image labels can describe different experimental conditions. Construct clear identifiers, inspect their structure and reject malformed records with reasons. Keep the original input and apply numerical QC rules set before looking at experimental groups.

scientific_context.caution: Image figure is authentic microscopy context, not raw calibrated fluorescence. IDs and QC metrics are entirely synthetic.

chapter_method: Learn → Apply → Prove on every mini-goal, then complete a strict identity/QC validator, explain failure cases, export a runnable Python script and return on another day for a different label convention.

goals.title: Build informative sample labels
goals.why: A sample label must continue to identify the right strain, plate and condition when the acquisition record changes.
explain: **Make labels from data rather than retyping them.** A specimen label is an identifier, not a measurement. Use Python f-strings to combine meaningful variables in a stable order. The two image records `N2_P03_control` and `N2_P03_heat` describe different conditions; a wrong suffix can invalidate a biological grouping.

**Normalize only what your naming policy permits.** `strip()` removes accidental leading/trailing whitespace; `upper()` and `lower()` standardize case. Here plate codes use uppercase `P`, and conditions use lowercase text. Strain names remain case-sensitive, so preserve their internal spelling rather than silently converting them.

**Choose an explicit grammar.** In this chapter a simple identifier has exactly three underscore-separated parts: `strain_P##_condition`. Allowed conditions will be `control`, `heat` or `recovery`. A later validator rejects unclear labels rather than guessing; do not silently rewrite the original raw identifier at that stage.

**An f-string is evaluated when the assignment runs.** Changing `condition` later does not update an older computed label until the formatting expression is rerun. This is the same stale-derived-value issue introduced in P01.

**Scientific caution:** names should point to recorded acquisition metadata, not be used to infer treatment or replicate identity from image appearance. Imaging fields are not independent biological replicates.

worked_example.code:
strain = 'N2'
plate = 'p03 '
condition = ' Heat '
label = f'{strain}_{plate.strip().upper()}_{condition.strip().lower()}'
print(label)
worked_example.predict: What exact label will print, and which characters are preserved?

goals.prediction_answer: `N2_P03_heat`. The plate and condition are normalized under the stated convention, but the strain string is preserved.
walkthrough: Check the values of strain, plate and condition before interpolation.
`plate.strip().upper()` removes the trailing space and makes P uppercase.
`condition.strip().lower()` turns ' Heat ' into 'heat'; the f-string joins the three pieces with underscores.
investigate: Change `condition` to `Control` and predict the suffix.
Change the strain from `N2` to `mutA`; verify its case remains unchanged.
Remove `strip()` and see why two labels that look similar may not be exact string matches.
goals.debug_task: A colleague writes `label = 'strain_plate_condition'`. Explain why it never changes when the experiment changes; repair the f-string.
goals.misconception: Words inside an ordinary quoted string are magically replaced by variable values.
goals.scientific_boundary: These are synthetic specimen records. Plate codes and treatment labels are not retrieved from a microscope image.

goals.title: Parse an identifier without guessing
goals.why: An unexpected extra underscore or missing plate must not be silently reassigned to another experimental group.
explain: **Parsing splits a record into parts.** `sample_id.split('_')` produces a Python list of text components. `len(parts)` counts how many parts were found. You do not need to know loops or general list algorithms to inspect this output.

**Structure is different from validity.** `N2_P03_heat` has three nonempty components; `N2_P03_heat_day2` has four; `N2__heat` has three but an empty plate. Checking only the number of separators is not enough. The full semantic checks appear in G04.

**Use `==` to compare values and `and` to combine Boolean conditions.** A condition such as `len(parts) == 3` produces True or False. Python evaluates the right side of `and` only when the left side is true, so you can check length before referencing individual pieces.

**Do not quietly repair raw source labels.** Stripping or rearranging a malformed ID at import time could overwrite provenance. Store the original label and return a clear failure classification; decide on normalization only at the controlled label-generation step.

**Delimiter choice matters.** The underscore is a reserved separator in this exercise. A strain name containing `_` must either use an explicit escaping policy or be rejected under this grammar. P02 chooses strict rejection, not guessing which segment belongs to the strain.

worked_example.predict: What list and number will be printed?

walkthrough: A separator divides one string into a list of smaller strings.
`len(parts)` reports the count, not whether the components make scientific sense.
Try missing and repeated separators. Three sections do not guarantee that every section contains text.
investigate: Replace `sample_id` with `N2__heat`. Why is the number of parts still three?

goals.debug_task: A lab script assumes anything with two underscores is valid. Show an empty-component counterexample that passes this naive test.
goals.misconception: Three components automatically means a correct scientific identifier.
goals.scientific_boundary: The format of a filename does not certify whether an underlying experiment was recorded or labeled correctly.

goals.title: Compare quantitative QC values safely
goals.why: An inclusive predeclared focus threshold must behave predictably at the boundary and with implausible values.
explain: **Comparisons return Boolean values.** `>=` means greater than or equal to; `>` excludes the boundary. `==` checks equality and is not the assignment operator `=`. A measurement exactly at the required minimum passes only when the declared policy is inclusive.

**Combine independent conditions.** `and` requires both criteria; `or` accepts either. A score of 1.2 should not be accepted simply because it exceeds a minimum if the documented score scale is 0–1. Python supports the readable chained comparison `0 <= score <= 1`.

**Numerical text is not automatically numerical measurement.** The string `'0.8'` must be deliberately converted with `float` before comparing with 0.8. Invalid text raises ValueError; automatic catch-and-replace would fabricate a QC result. P05 teaches controlled exception handling.

**Thresholds must be set before inspecting experimental groups.** A training score of 0.8 and a training minimum of 0.8 are invented values. They are not recommendations for microscope autofocus, imaging quality or biological sample exclusion.

**Boundary and edge tests are essential.** Test below, at and above the minimum; outside the supported range; and cases where maximum thresholds differ. A program can execute correctly while embedding a biased or scientifically unsuitable QC cutoff.

focus_score = 0.80
minimum_focus = 0.80
print(focus_score >= minimum_focus)
print(focus_score > minimum_focus)
print(0 <= focus_score <= 1)

goals.misconception: Passing a numerical threshold automatically means the biological image is good quality.
goals.scientific_boundary: All scores are fictional. No numerical cutoff is validated for a particular acquisition protocol or biological model.

goals.title: Explain QC decisions with conditions
goals.why: A trustworthy validator rejects invalid labels or low-quality records with a reproducible reason, not just a yes/no verdict.
explain: **Use a documented decision order.** Python's `if`, `elif`, `else` evaluates conditions from top to bottom; the first matching branch determines what happens. Validate label structure *before* indexing its parts, then check known fields, then the numerical rule.

**Do not collapse all failures to False.** A missing label component is a data-integrity problem; a correctly labeled observation below a focus threshold is a different exclusion reason. In P02 the decision is `ACCEPT` or `REJECT` with a specific plain-language `reason`.

**Check exact boundaries and condition names.** An equality at the declared minimum passes an inclusive criterion. Labels are case-sensitive on import; `control` is valid, `Control` is not. The formatter in G01 can normalize new labels, but importing historical records must preserve raw input for audit.

**Explain a branch without guessing.** The condition `len(parts) != 3` must come first; only then is it safe to read `parts[0]`, `parts[1]` and `parts[2]`. You can use `not` to reverse a condition and `or` to combine several rejection reasons.

**Reject scientifically invalid assumptions.** Changing cutoffs to make one experimental group look better is not quality control. Apply one predeclared rule consistently and document acquisition-level quality metrics separately from biological interpretation.

worked_example.code:
sample_id = 'N2_P03_control'
focus_score = 0.80
minimum_focus = 0.80
parts = sample_id.split('_')
if len(parts) != 3:
    decision = 'REJECT'
    reason = 'wrong number of fields'
elif focus_score < minimum_focus:
    decision = 'REJECT'
    reason = 'focus below minimum'
else:
    decision = 'ACCEPT'
    reason = 'label shape and focus acceptable'
print(decision, reason)
worked_example.predict: Does a score exactly equal to the minimum pass, and what happens with a fourth underscore-separated field?

goals.prediction_answer: At equality it accepts because the rejection test uses `<`. Four fields cause `REJECT` with `wrong number of fields` even if focus is high.
walkthrough: Inspect `parts = sample_id.split('_')` before accessing any segment.
The first branch rejects structurally malformed input, so the score is not interpreted for a bad label.
The second branch compares focus against the predeclared minimum; equality flows to the accepting `else` branch.
investigate: Change the sample to `N2_P03_control_extra` and identify the first matching branch.
Change focus_score to 0.79 and verify the reason is specifically focus-related.
Change focus_score back to the exact boundary 0.80; it should accept. Then try `N2__heat` and note that the simple demonstration does not yet check empty fields—the capstone will.
goals.debug_task: A lab script replaces all rejected records with reason `bad image`. Explain why this prevents distinguishing a mislabeled record from an out-of-focus record.
goals.misconception: An accepted focus score certifies sample condition or biological validity.
goals.scientific_boundary: Example QC thresholds are synthetic, not real instrument cutoffs. A valid label does not imply that underlying biology or image intensities are valid.

capstone.title: Specimen intake validator — complete chapter project
capstone.why: Prevent sample misassignment and make quality exclusion decisions traceable.
capstone.scientific_boundary: Toy labels and numeric focus scores are synthetic. The 0–1 example score and thresholds are not established microscopy QC standards; do not use them to exclude real biological data.
explain: **Research task:** Two visually similar filenames may encode different experimental conditions. Build one repeatable intake checker that accepts only syntactically valid sample IDs and predeclared focus scores and writes a transparent reason for rejection.

**Fixed identifier grammar:** `strain_P##_condition`, with exactly two underscores. The strain contains **one or more ASCII alphanumeric characters** (A–Z, a–z, 0–9) and no spaces; the plate is an uppercase P followed by exactly two ASCII digits; accepted conditions are exactly `control`, `heat`, `recovery`. Do not normalize or rewrite raw identifiers while validating: preserve the original `sample_id`.

**Declared focus rule:** score is a numeric value from 0 through 1 inclusive; the minimum_focus is supplied before evaluation. Scores equal to the minimum are accepted. Invalid shape, invalid strain, invalid plate, unknown condition, invalid score range and low score have distinct reason strings, in that order.

**Validation-method toolkit:** `.startswith('P')` asks whether a plate code begins with uppercase P. `len(plate) == 3` demands exactly three characters. `.removeprefix('P')` returns the remaining characters when P is present. `.isdigit()` checks digit characters, while `.isascii()` rules out lookalike Unicode numerals under this chapter's deliberately ASCII-only grammar. Combine these checks; one alone is insufficient.

**A small executable probe before the final validator:** `plate = 'P03'`; inspect `plate.startswith('P')`, `len(plate)`, `plate.removeprefix('P')`, and `plate.removeprefix('P').isascii() and plate.removeprefix('P').isdigit()`. Then change the plate to `Px3`, `P3`, `p03`, and `P３3`. Only the original should satisfy every declared check.

**Safe access to parsed fields:** `parts = sample_id.split('_')` creates a list. Position 0 is the strain, position 1 the plate, and position 2 the condition. Access these indices only *after* verifying `len(parts) == 3`; otherwise an incomplete input can trigger `IndexError` rather than an informative rejection. This limited indexing is introduced here for validation; full list operations will come in P03.

**Case priority matters.** Check three components before extracting them. If a field contains an underscore, the structure is invalid under this grammar. If the sample ID is malformed, label integrity takes precedence over focus; do not call it an imaging-quality failure.

**Deliverable:** `decision` (`ACCEPT` or `REJECT`), a specific `reason`, and a human-readable `report` containing the unmodified raw ID, decision and reason. Print the report; export the runnable script. Provide a written reflection on false positives, off-by-one boundaries and why imaging fields differ from biological replicates.

**Independent transfer:** Apply the same principles to an unfamiliar record grammar with pipe separators and `F##` acquisition codes. Reconstruct validation and explicit reasons without looking at the worked example.

**Limitations:** A clean label and focus score do not establish genuine specimen identity, raw image quality, biological validity or instrument calibration. In research you must verify metadata provenance and preregister relevant exclusion rules.

capstone.debug_task: A copied script accepts `N2_Px3_heat` because its only QC criterion is the number of underscores. Identify the missing semantic check and the risk of assigning a plate incorrectly.

# TASK: Validate specimen|F##|treatment and quality; set verdict, explanation,
#   result_line.
# RULE: Preserve raw ID; follow exact reason priority in panel.
# INPUTS: record_id, quality_score, threshold

practice_feedback.why: Transfer replaces plate IDs with acquisition IDs, yet still requires an explicit reason for every rejected record.
practice_feedback.probe: Try `N2_Px3_heat`, `_P03_heat`, `N2_P03_Heat`, and a low-focus valid record.
practice_feedback.check: Probe `P03`, `Px3`, `P3` and `P３3` with `.startswith`, `.removeprefix`, `.isascii` and `.isdigit` to understand each syntactic requirement.

build_steps: PASS 1 — Split and count first. Test N2_P03_heat versus N2_P03_heat_more. An extra segment must be rejected as 'expected three fields' before indexing.
PASS 2 — Verify a nonempty ASCII-alphanumeric strain. Try _P03_heat and mut-A_P03_heat; both must report 'invalid strain'.
PASS 3 — Require uppercase P plus two ASCII digits. Compare P03 with p03, P3, Px3 and a Unicode digit lookalike; invalid codes must report 'invalid plate'.
PASS 4 — Match control, heat or recovery exactly, without silently normalizing the raw ID. N2_P03_Heat must report 'unknown condition'.
PASS 5 — Validate numerical scores against synthetic 0..1 before the inclusive minimum. At a minimum of 0.8, 1.2 is invalid, 0.79 is low and 0.8 passes.
PASS 6 — Return only the first failure in the declared order and construct the exact report. Run all Apply cases before independently handling the new pipe-separated grammar in Prove.

review.title: Later recall — unfamiliar labeled acquisitions
review.why: Reconstruct string validation and conditional QC on a later day without copying a previous program.
review.scientific_boundary: All data and thresholds are illustrative; no automatic claim of long-term retention or validated microscopy acquisition QC.
explain: **Retrieval without recognition:** Rebuild a validator on an unfamiliar naming policy rather than rereading the capstone. Attempt after at least 24 hours for delayed practice, but an earlier practice attempt is allowed.

**New convention:** labels are in the form `strain~S##~condition`, with exactly three nonempty segments and ASCII alphanumeric strain, `S` plus two ASCII digits, and condition equal to control, heat or recovery.

**Same scientific discipline:** report exact rejection reasons and apply a predeclared inclusive quality threshold to numeric 0–1 scores. A passing code test does not certify that a real biological record is valid.

worked_example.predict: How would you distinguish a malformed label from a below-threshold score, without inspecting previous code?

review.prediction_answer: Validate the structural grammar and permitted components before comparing a predeclared score cutoff.
walkthrough: Recall `.split`, conditional branches and `>=` without opening old answers.
Write down the input grammar and precise reason priority.
Solve on changed data and record whether help was used.
investigate: Try before reopening the prior chapter.
Explain how a plausible label could still reference the wrong physical specimen.
review.misconception: Remembering the shape of the earlier answer equals independent mastery.
review.debug_task: Explain why changing the threshold after viewing results is not a valid fix for high rejection rates.

feedback.IndexError: Never index pieces before checking the segment count.
feedback.NameError: Inspect new variable names; they differ from the preceding capstone.
feedback.hardcoded: The return task uses changed values and a new grammar.

reflection_prompts: What checks did you write from memory?
Which error case was most difficult, and did you use help?
What makes this QC policy scientifically defensible or not?
